newsitem.title: NIGERIA: African troops said combat ready on Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: African troops said combat ready on Sierra Leone.

text.p: Nigerian-led African peacekeeping troops stationed in Sierra Leone are ready to drive out soldiers who seized power there, according to the commander of the West African ECOMOG force, Major-General Victor Malu.
"We have the capability of flushing out those people if and when we are directed to do so," Malu, a Nigerian, told reporters on arrival at Lagos airport on Tuesday.

Nigeria said last week it was not contemplating withdrawing its troops which dominate the force, whose stated aim is to reverse the May 25 coup by junior army officers who toppled the elected president, Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

Kabbah fled to neighbouring Guinea's capital Conakry, where West African foreign ministers met last week and decided on a three-pronged approach of dialogue, sanctions and force to end the Sierra Leone coup.

They set up a committee comprising the foreign ministers of Nigeria, Guinea, Ghana and Ivory Coast to persuade Sierra Leone's new rulers to restore Kabbah and to report to the chairman of the Economic Community of West African States Nigeria's General Sani Abacha within two weeks on the outcome.
"The decisions taken are to be put in place one after the other," said Malu.

"If after two weeks of consultation they report to the chairman that these people are still adamant in reversing the situation as it is supposed to be then all those measures can be applied at the same time," he added.

Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on June 2 and Nigerian soldiers were in turn attacked by Sierra Leone forces and their Revolutionary United Front (RUF) rebel allies at a hotel where the Nigerians were guarding foreigners.

A widely expected Nigerian military attack has since not materialised and Nigerian military sources said any decision to attack would be taken after the expiration of the two weeks of consultations with the Sierra Leonean rulers.
"The two weeks end around July 10," said one.
